report.source_text: Two weeks later, the patient underwent thoracoscopic resection of the left lung cancer. Macroscopic examination revealed that the excised 14×9.5×3.5-cm upper left lobe included a 3.1×2.5×2-cm mass with gray and grayish black sections, solid, medium in texture, and indistinct from the surrounding boundary (Fig. 3). The mass was adjacent to the pleura and did not involve the bronchus. Histologically, the tumor cells were moderately to poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma of the acinar and micropapillary type (Fig. 4A-D), and no cryptococcal infection was observed. No metastatic cancer was found in the lymph nodes (0/11), the bronchial incisive margin was negative and the pathological TNM stage was T2aN0Mx.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 65-year-old asymptomatic Han Chinese woman who worked as a crop farmer presented to Taihe Hospital in August 2018 for routine physical examination. Chest CT imaging revealed two separate left lung nodules: a 2.4×2.0 cm nodule in the anterior segment of the left superior lobe (initially suspected to be peripheral lung cancer) and a 1.3×0.9 cm nodule in the posterior basal segment of the left lower lobe (initially suspected to be intrapulmonary metastasis). Approximately 1 week after imaging, a CT-guided percutaneous lung biopsy was performed on the smaller left lower lobe nodule. Histopathology revealed granulomatous inflammation and yeast-form fungi in multinucleated cells, with cryptococcus identified by periodic acid Schiff (PAS), Gomori methenamine silver (GMS), and mucicarmine (MC) staining, confirming cryptococcal infection. Two weeks after the initial imaging, the patient underwent thoracoscopic resection of the left upper lobe, which revealed the larger nodule to be moderately to poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma (T2aN0Mx) with no cryptococcal infection. Following the biopsy diagnosis of cryptococcal infection, the patient received fluconazole 200 mg/day for 6 months. Over 5 years of follow-up imaging (every 6 months for the first 2 years, then annually for the last 3 years), with the latest follow-up in August 2023, contrast-enhanced CT showed no recurrence of either disease, and the patient remained in good condition.
